title: QROS blocker / backlog row
description: Validates a single row of templates/backlog.md (QROS 2.0.0). Enforces QROS-BLOCKER-CLASSES, QROS-BLOCKER-ADMISSION, QROS-REVIEW-SELF-REPORTED-NOT-BLOCKING and QROS-BLOCKER-CLOSED-STAYS-CLOSED. Three genuinely different row shapes are discriminated on `class` rather than merged, so that a non-blocking backlog row is never required to carry a fabricated threat class or failure path, and a transport failure is never recorded as a finding against the work.

oneOf.title: Blocking row
oneOf.$comment: QROS-BLOCKER-ADMISSION: admitted only with a named threat AND a concrete failure path on the current or next stage. `threat_class` optionally tags the threat with the closed QROS-THREAT-VOCABULARY. A SELF-REPORTED statement never blocks on its own, so the row's evidence is REPRODUCED or REASONED. `evidence_to_clear` is required so every row has a defined exit; a row that cannot be closed is not admissible.

allOf.$comment: QROS-BLOCKER-CLOSED-STAYS-CLOSED: a closed row keeps the evidence that closed it.

oneOf.title: Non-blocking backlog row
oneOf.$comment: A different shape by design. `threat`, `threat_class` and `failure_path` are PROHIBITED here, not merely optional, so the blocker/backlog distinction cannot be eroded by filling a blocker shape with invented values.

kind.description: Free project vocabulary. Deliberately NOT the threat vocabulary: a backlog row names no threat.

oneOf.title: Unsatisfied-gate row
oneOf.$comment: QROS-BLOCKER-TRANSPORT-NOT-IMPLEMENTATION: a transport, tool, packaging, review-seat or procedural failure leaves a gate unsatisfied, is not evidence of an implementation defect, and consumes no review round. It carries no threat and no failure path, because none was demonstrated.
